:::note[Written against main]
This page follows `main` at cbe2c19, and it differs from the copy in HotLoop Cascade 0.1.2, the latest release. Parts of it may be newer than what you have installed. The [release notes](/releases/) say what moved.
:::

On a Podman host, `deploy/quadlet` has systemd units. One file and a volume is
Cascade on SQLite; `deploy/quadlet/postgres` is the server, a worker and
PostgreSQL on a network of their own. Both start at boot, restart on failure and
run read-only, nonroot, with every capability dropped. Its README walks through
it.

To pull a version by hand:

```sh
podman pull ghcr.io/hotloop-io/hotloop-cascade:0.1.2
```

The units follow `:stable` and Podman's auto-update timer moves them.

On k3s, `charts/hotloop-cascade` is the Helm chart:

```sh
helm install cascade oci://ghcr.io/hotloop-io/charts/hotloop-cascade --version 0.1.2
```

That is one pod on SQLite with a volume. `--set split=true` with PostgreSQL
(`--set postgresql.enabled=true` for one the chart runs, or
`externalDatabase.existingSecret` for yours) splits it into API, webhook and
worker pods that you scale on their own. The key that seals stored credentials
is made on the first install and kept when the release is uninstalled, because
a key that goes with the release takes every credential in a kept database with
it. Back it up.

`hotloop-cascade healthcheck` asks the running server's own health endpoint and
exits 0 or 1. The Quadlet units and the chart's probes both use the endpoints
behind it.
